chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is nothing fixed regarding the recitation except for Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun.
ai.seo_question: What are the specific Surahs required to be recited in the Friday prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the obligatory nature of reciting Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun in the two-rak'ah Friday prayer, a ruling derived from the Prophet's practice and affirmed by Shia jurists. The selection is thematically significant, as both chapters highlight the themes of divine sovereignty, the hypocrisy of the unfaithful, and the gathering for worship, thereby reinforcing the spiritual and communal identity of the Friday congregation.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is nothing fixed regarding the recitation except for the Friday. You should recite with the (Surah) Al-Jummah (Chapter 62), and the (Surah) Al-Munafiqeen (Chapter 63)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The recitation is not definite texts except on Friday in which there is Surah (chapter) al-Jumu‘ah and al-Munafiqun.’”
